title: Search in BST
description: Given a BST in level-order form using -1 for nulls and a target value, return whether the target exists in the tree.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
intendedApproachSummary: Compare against the current node and move only left or right using BST ordering.
wrongApproachHints: Do not recurse into both children for a BST search.
Moving in the wrong direction after a comparison loses the logarithmic path behavior.
hints: If target is smaller, go left.
If target is larger, go right.

examples.explanation: 5 lies in the right subtree of 4 and the left subtree of 6.

functionContract.javaSignature: public boolean searchBST(TreeNode root, int target)

title: Inorder Traversal of BST
description: Given a BST in level-order form using -1 for nulls, print its inorder traversal.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
intendedApproachSummary: Traverse left subtree, visit root, then traverse right subtree so the output becomes sorted.
wrongApproachHints: Preorder or postorder will not give sorted BST output.
The current node belongs between the two recursive calls.
hints: Inorder means left, root, right.
Notice the sorted order in the final output.

examples.explanation: A BST's inorder traversal is sorted.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given a binary tree, print Valid if it satisfies BST ordering everywhere, otherwise print Invalid.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
edgeCases: A deep descendant breaks an ancestor bound
Duplicate values invalidate strict BST ordering
intendedApproachSummary: Carry valid low and high bounds through recursion so every node is checked against global constraints.
wrongApproachHints: Checking only parent-child order is not enough.
An inorder list is useful, but you still need strict ascending order.
hints: Each left subtree node must stay below the current node.
Each right subtree node must stay above it.

examples.explanation: Every node respects the global BST range rules.

title: Insert into BST
description: Given a BST and a value x, insert x and print the inorder traversal after insertion.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
edgeCases: Insert as a leaf on either side
intendedApproachSummary: Walk down the BST until the correct null child is found, then attach the new node there.
wrongApproachHints: Do not rebuild the entire tree.
Preserve all existing child links during recursion.
hints: Go left for smaller values and right for larger values.
Return the root pointer back up the recursion.

functionContract.javaSignature: public TreeNode insertBST(TreeNode root, int x)

title: Floor and Ceil in BST
description: Given a BST and a target value, print the floor and ceil values. If one side does not exist, print -1 for it.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
outputFormat: Print floor and ceil separated by a space
intendedApproachSummary: Track the best lower and best upper candidate while descending only one branch at a time.
wrongApproachHints: Do not collect and sort all nodes.
Update floor and ceil only when the current node improves them.
hints: A smaller current value can improve the floor.
A larger current value can improve the ceil.

examples.explanation: 4 is the greatest value below 5 and 6 is the smallest value above 5.

functionContract.javaSignature: public List<Integer> floorCeilBST(TreeNode root, int target)

title: Lowest Common Ancestor in BST
description: Given a BST and two node values p and q, print the value of their lowest common ancestor.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
edgeCases: One target is the ancestor of the other
Targets lie on different sides of the root
intendedApproachSummary: If both values are smaller, go left. If both are larger, go right. Otherwise the current node is the answer.
wrongApproachHints: You do not need a full general-binary-tree LCA traversal here.
Stop as soon as the two targets split.
hints: Compare both p and q with the current node.
The split point is the LCA.

examples.explanation: 2 is on the left of 6 and 8 is on the right.

functionContract.javaSignature: public int lowestCommonAncestorBST(TreeNode root, int p, int q)
functionContract.cppSignature: int lowestCommonAncestorBST(TreeNode* root, int p, int q)

title: Kth Smallest Element in BST
description: Given a BST and an integer k, print the kth smallest value in the tree.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
edgeCases: k is the number of nodes
intendedApproachSummary: Perform inorder traversal and count visited nodes until the kth one is reached.
wrongApproachHints: Do not sort an extra array if inorder already gives sorted order.
Counting in preorder gives the wrong answer.
hints: Inorder visits values from smallest to largest.
Stop as soon as count reaches k.

functionContract.javaSignature: public int kthSmallestBST(TreeNode root, int k)

title: Inorder Successor in BST
description: Given a BST and a target value guaranteed to exist, print its inorder successor or -1 if it does not exist.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
intendedApproachSummary: Move down the tree while tracking the best larger candidate encountered so far.
wrongApproachHints: Do not assume the parent is always the successor.
The answer may lie above the target rather than in its right child.
hints: Whenever you go left from a larger node, that node is a successor candidate.
Going right cannot improve the current successor candidate.

examples.explanation: 7 is the next larger value after 6.

functionContract.javaSignature: public int inorderSuccessorBST(TreeNode root, int target)

title: Range Sum of BST
description: Given a BST and a range [low, high], print the sum of all node values within the range.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
edgeCases: All nodes are outside the range
Only one subtree can contain valid values
intendedApproachSummary: Use BST ordering to prune any subtree that falls completely below low or above high.
wrongApproachHints: Do not traverse both subtrees blindly when one side is impossible.
Only add the current node when it lies inside the range.
hints: If root.val < low, skip the entire left subtree.
If root.val > high, skip the entire right subtree.

examples.explanation: The values 7, 10, and 15 are inside the range.

title: Delete Node in BST
description: Given a BST and a key, delete that key and print the inorder traversal after deletion.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
intendedApproachSummary: Handle the zero-child, one-child, and two-child cases. For two children, replace with successor and then delete the successor node.
wrongApproachHints: You cannot just remove a node with children.
Be careful not to lose subtrees during reconnection.
hints: Find the inorder successor in the right subtree.
Delete the successor after copying its value.

examples.explanation: 3 is removed while preserving BST order.

title: Trim BST to Range
description: Given a BST and bounds [low, high], trim away nodes outside the range and print the inorder traversal of the remaining tree.
inputFormat: n level-order values with -1 for null
outputFormat: Print inorder traversal of the trimmed BST
intendedApproachSummary: Use BST pruning rules to drop impossible subtrees and reconnect the surviving children.
wrongApproachHints: Do not keep a node that lies outside the allowed range.
You can replace the root directly with a valid child subtree when needed.
hints: If root.val < low, only the right subtree can survive.
If root.val > high, only the left subtree can survive.
